title: Level 1 (Beginner) - B-12
notes:
West leads the ♠Q against 4♥. At a suit contract, West would not lead the ♠Q from a holding containing the ♠A. South, thus, has nothing to gain from playing the ♠K from dummy. On the given layout, it doesn't matter. The defense takes 3 spade tricks and plays a club won with the ♣A.

South must avoid losing a trick to the ♦K and should finesse East for that card. As East may have the ♦K well guarded, South should take a diamond finesse each time he is in the dummy.

After finessing diamonds, South should cash a trump trick in the closed hand before crossing to dummy in trumps. Cashing a round of trumps before crossing to the dummy is a safety play against West holding 2 hearts and a singleton diamond.

A second diamond finesse is taken. The dummy still has a trump entry to take a third diamond finesse.
